He sent from on high and received me, and he gave over to reproach those who trample me; God sent forth his mercy and his truth.
And he delivered my soul from among the beasts, for I slept in anxiety. The sons of men: their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongues are like sharpened swords.
You are exalted in the heavens, O God, and your glory is over all the earth.
They prepared a snare for my feet and brought my soul low. They dug a pit before me, and they themselves fell into it.
My heart is ready for you, O God; my heart is ready to bless and to sing of your glory.
Awake, my glory; awake with psalm and blessing, and I will awake at dawn.
I will confess you among the people, O Lord, and I will sing to you among the nations.
For your mercy has been made great up to the heavens, and your truth reaches to the clouds.
You are exalted in the heavens, O God, and your glory is over all the earth.
If only you would truly speak righteousness and judge what is right, O sons of men!
But now, rather, in your heart you commit lawlessness on the earth, and your hands fashion falsehood.
Sinners have become estranged from the mother; they went astray from the womb and spoke falsehood.
Their serpent's wrath is like that of a serpent, like an asp and a deaf viper whose ears are stopped.
For it does not hear the voice of the skilled enchanter, nor does it accept a remedy from the wise administerer of drugs.
God has crushed their teeth in their mouth, and the Lord has ground up the jaw-teeth of the lions.
May they become contemptible, like water poured out; and at the drawing of their bow may they grow weak.
Like wax that melts, so may they be consumed. Fire fell upon them, and they did not see the sun.
Before their thorn has yet [?], and as with a bramble, in wrath, [?] them alive.
Let the righteous rejoice when he sees vengeance; he has washed his hands in the blood of the sinner.
Let a man say: Truly there is fruit for the righteous; and there is a God who judges them on the earth.
Deliver me from my enemies, O God, and rescue me from those who have risen up against me.
Deliver me from the workers of lawlessness, and save me from men of blood.
For behold, they have hunted my soul, and the mighty have attacked me; not for my lawlessness, nor for my sin.
Without sin I ran and went straight; awake before me and see.
And you, Lord God of hosts, God of Israel, see and attend to all the nations, and do not show favor to any who work lawlessness.
Let them return at evening, let them hunger [?] like dogs, and let them surround the city.
They speak with their mouth, and a sword is on their lips! Who has heard this?
But you, Lord, laughed at them, and you despised all the nations.
I will keep my strength for you, for you are God my helper,
my God, for his mercy hastened to me; may my God show me what concerns my enemies.
Do not destroy them, so that they may not forget your law; scatter them by your power and bring them down, for you are my protector, O Lord.
The prayer of their mouth and the words of their lips: let them be swallowed up in their pride, for they recount cursing and falsehood.
At the end let them be destroyed in wrath, let them be found no more; let them understand that God rules over Jacob and over all the ends of the earth.
Let them return at evening, let them hunger [?] like dogs, and let them surround the city.
Let them be scattered to eat; if they are not satisfied, let them even murmur.
But I will praise your power, and I will rejoice at dawn in your mercy; for you have been my protector and my refuge in the day of my affliction.
My helper, to you I will sing, O God, my protector, God of my life.
O God, you have scattered us and laid us waste; you were angry with us, and now have mercy on us.
You have shaken the earth and made it tremble; heal its breaches, for it has been moved.
You have shown your people your harshness; you gave us the wine of sorrow to drink.
You have given a sign to those who fear you, so that they may escape from the face of the bow.
So that you may deliver those who love you, save me with your right hand, and hear me.
God spoke from his holy place: I will rejoice and be exalted; I will divide Shechem and measure out the valley of dwellings.
Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the strengthener of my head; Judah is my king;
Moab is the basin of my hope; into Edom I will direct my going, and foreign peoples have submitted to me.
Who will bring me to the fortified city? Or who will lead me as far as Idumea?
Is it not you, God, who scattered us, and did not go out, God, in power for us?
Give us help in affliction, for vain is the salvation of man.
Through God let us do mightily, and he will bring to contempt all who afflict my soul.
Let my prayer be heard by God; look, O God, upon my prayer.
From the ends of the earth I cried out to you, until my heart grew weary. Lift me up upon a rock, lead me.
And be my hope, a strong tower before the face of the enemy.
I will dwell in your dwellings forever, I will take shelter in the shelter of your wings.
But you, God, hear my prayer, and give an inheritance to those who fear your name.
Day by day add to the king his years, until the day, from generation to generation.
He will abide before God forever; mercy and truth, who will seek them from him?
Thus I will sing to your name forever and ever, and I will render my prayers to you day by day.
But submit to God, my soul, for from him is my salvation.
For he is God, my Savior, my refuge, and I will not be shaken any more.
How long will you set upon men and kill them, all of you, as if they were a leaning wall and a fence pushed away?
But they plotted the removal of my honor, and they ran in their thirst; with their mouth they blessed and with their heart they cursed.
But you, submit to God alone, my soul, for from him is my endurance.
For from God is my salvation and my glory.
The God of my help, and my hope is in him.
Hope in him, all the assembly of the people; pour out your hearts before him, for God is our helper.
But vain are the sons of men, false are the sons of men upon that scale of falsehood, and they themselves are in vanity together.
Do not trust in falsehood, and do not set your heart on robbery; if wealth overflows to you, do not fasten your hearts on it.
Once God spoke, and these two things we heard: that strength belongs to God.
And from you, Lord, is mercy, and you will repay each person according to their deeds.
God, my God, to you I rise at dawn; my soul thirsts for you. How many times does this my flesh thirst for you, as in a desert land, pathless and waterless?
Thus in the holy place I appeared before you, that I might see your power and your glory.
For your mercy is better to me than lives, and my lips shall praise you.
Thus I shall sing to you, O my life, and in your name I shall lift up my hands to you.
As with the fat of richness let my soul be filled, and with lips of song my mouth shall praise you.
If I remembered you upon my bed, at dawn I would rise early and entreat you;
for you have been my helper, and in the shelter of your wings I shall rejoice.
My soul followed after you, and your right hand received me.
But they sought my soul in vain; they shall go down to the lowest depths of the earth.
They shall be given over to the hands of the sword; they shall be a portion for foxes.
But the king shall rejoice in God, and all who swear by him shall be [?], for the mouth that spoke falsehood has been stopped.
Hear, O God, my prayer when I pray to you; deliver my soul from fear of the enemy.
Shelter me from the assembly of the wicked and from the multitude of the workers of lawlessness,
who have sharpened their tongues like swords; they have bent their bow with a bitter deed,
to shoot in darkness, in secret, at the upright in heart; suddenly they shot arrows at them, and they were not afraid.
They strengthened for themselves an evil word; they plotted the laying of a snare, and they said: Who will see us?
They searched out their iniquities; they devised the searching out of the things to be searched out. A man shall stand forth with the depth of his heart,
and God shall be exalted. The arrows of infants have become their wounds.
Their tongues have grown weak against them. All who saw them were shaken.
And every man was afraid. They declared the works of God and understood his creatures.
Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord, hope in him, and let all the upright in heart boast in him.
To you, O God, song is fitting in Zion, and to you prayer shall be rendered in Jerusalem.
Hear my prayer; to you all people shall come.
The words of the lawless have prevailed over me, and be merciful to me for my sins.
Blessed is the one whom you have chosen. Receive him, and he shall dwell in your courts. We have been filled with the good things of your house; holy is your temple,
wondrous [?] in righteousness. Hear me, O God our Savior, hope of all the ends of the earth and of those who are far off on the sea.
who prepares the mountains by his strength and has girded them with might,
who shakes the wealth of the sea and calms the roar of its waves. The nations shall be shaken,
and those who dwell on the earth shall be afraid of your signs, O Lord; at the going forth of morning and evening they shall rejoice.
Look upon the earth, make it drunk, multiply its enrichment; the river of God is filled with water; you have prepared their food, for [?] is the preparation.
Make its furrows drunk, multiply its fruit; by your dew its sprouts shall rejoice.
You will bless the crown of the year with your sweetness, and your fields shall be filled with fatness.
The beauty of the wilderness shall grow fat, and the hills shall clothe themselves with joy.
The rams of the sheep are clothed, the valleys shall multiply wheat; they shall cry out and sing.
Cry out to God, all the earth.
Sing to his name, give glory to his praise.
Say to God: How fearful are your works! Through the greatness of your power your enemies shall lie to you.
Let all the earth worship you and sing to you, and let them sing to your name.
Come and see the works of God, how fearful he is in his counsel, more than the sons of men,
who turned the sea into dry land, and they crossed the river on foot; there let us rejoice in him,
who rules by his power forever. His eyes look upon the nations; let those who embitter him not be exalted in themselves.
Bless our God, you nations, and make the voice of his praise heard,
who has set our soul in life and has not allowed our feet to be shaken.
You have tested us, O God, and you have refined us as silver is refined.
You have brought us into the snare, you have gathered affliction upon our shoulders,
and you have sent a man over our heads. We passed through fire and water, and you have brought us out into your place of rest.
I will enter your house with a sacrifice and I will give you my vows,
which my lips vowed, which I spoke with my mouth in my affliction.
I will offer you a sacrifice full of marrow, together with rams and incense; I will offer you young bulls and goats.
Come and hear me, and I will tell all of you who fear God what he has done for my soul.
For to him I cried out with my mouth, and I exalted him with my tongue.
If I regard sin in my heart, do not listen, O Lord.
Therefore the Lord has heard me and has attended to the voice of my prayer.
Blessed is the Lord, who has not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.
O God, have mercy on us and bless us; show your face upon us and have mercy on us,
that your way may be known on the earth and your salvation among all the nations.
Let the peoples confess you, O God; let all the peoples confess you.
Let the nations be glad and rejoice, for you will judge the people with righteousness, and you will guide the nations on the earth.
Let the peoples confess you, O God; let all the peoples confess you.
The earth has yielded its fruit; may God, our God, bless us.
May God bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear him.
Let God arise, and let all his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his face.
As smoke fades away, let them fade away, and as wax melts before fire, so let sinners perish from the face of God.
And let the righteous rejoice; let them be glad before God and exult with joy.
Bless God and sing to his name; make way for him who sits upon the west. Lord is his name, and rejoice before him.
Tremble before the face of him who is the father of orphans and the judge of widows; God is in his holy place.
God settles those of one manner of life in a name [? probably an error for 'house']; he brings out those in bonds by his strength; likewise those who embitter him, who lie asleep in the tombs.
O God, when you went out before your people and when you passed through the wilderness,
the earth shook, and the heavens too dripped before the face of the God of Sinai, before the face of the God of Israel.
You prepared a voluntary rain, O God, for your inheritance; though it grew weak, you strengthened it again.
And your living creatures dwell in it; in your sweetness you have made provision for the poor, O God.
The Lord will give the word to those who bring good news with great power.
The King of the hosts of the beloved; the beauty of your house is to divide the spoils.
If you sleep among the portions, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, and the middle of its back with the color of gold.
When the one who is in the heavens appointed kings over it, they were made white as snow on Selmon.
The mountain of God is a rich mountain, a mountain joined together [?] and a rich mountain.
Why do you imagine such things, you joined-together mountains? This is the mountain on which it pleased God to dwell, for the Lord too will dwell on it completely.
The chariots of God are ten-thousandfold, and thousands drive them onward; the Lord is among them, in his holy Sinai.
He went up on high, he took captives, he received them and distributed them as gifts to men, so that there may be a dwelling-place even for unbelievers.
The Lord God is blessed; blessed is God day by day. May the God of our salvation lead us onward.
Our God is a God who saves, and from the Lord are the ways out of death.
But God will crush the heads of his enemies, the crown with its hair, of those who walk in their lawlessness.
God said: From Bashan I will turn them back and bring them from the depths of the sea,
so that your feet may be soaked in blood, and the tongues of your dogs in the blood of his enemies.
Your processions have appeared, O God, the processions of God and our King, who is in the holy place.
The rulers hastened to offer song, among the maidens who give praise.
In the church bless God and the Lord, from the fountains of Israel.
There is Benjamin the youth, in amazement; the rulers of Judah, his leaders; the rulers of Zebulun and the rulers of Naphtali.
Command, O God, by your power; strengthen this which you have strengthened for yourself.
From your holy temple, from Jerusalem, kings will offer gifts to you.
Rage against the beasts of the reeds, the assembly of bulls and heifers among the people, so that those who have been tested with silver may bow down. Scatter the nations that desire war.
Let envoys come from Egypt, and let the Indians hasten to give their hand to God.
Kings of the earth, bless God and sing to his name,
to him who ascended to the heaven of heavens from the east. Behold, he has given forth his voice, the voice of his might.
Give glory to God; his splendor is great over Israel, and his power is in the clouds.
God is wonderful among his holy ones. The God of Israel, he will give power and strength to his people; blessed is God.
Save me, O God, for the waters have entered into my soul.
I have sunk into the depth of the abysses, where there was no rest; I came into the depth of the sea, and the surging tide has drowned me.
I have grown weary with my crying out, and my voice has broken; [?] my eyes, through hoping in the Lord my God.
Those who hate me without cause have become more numerous than the hairs of my head; my pursuers and my enemies have grown strong through falsehood; what I had not seized, I was then repaying.
O God, you know my foolishness, and my sins have not been hidden from you.
Let those who wait for you, O Lord, Lord of hosts, not be ashamed because of me; and let those who seek you, O God of Israel, not be disgraced on my account.
For it is for your sake that I have endured reproach; shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers and a guest to the sons of my mother.
For zeal for your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen upon me.
I humbled my soul with fasting, and that became a reproach to me.
I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sat in the gates talked about me, and those who drank wine sang about me.
But I prayed to you; it is the time of favor. O God, in your great mercy hear me, in the truth of your salvation.
Deliver me from the mud, so that I may not sink; let me escape from those who hate me and from the depths of many waters.
Let the whirlpool of waters not swallow me, nor the depth of the abysses cover me, nor the pit close its mouth over me.
Hear me, O Lord, for your mercy is sweet; O God, in your great compassion look upon me.
Do not turn your face away from your servant, for I am in distress; hear me quickly.
Attend to my soul, rescue it, and deliver me from my enemies.
For you know my reproach, my shame, and my disgrace; all who afflict my soul are before you.
My soul has endured reproach and poverty; I waited for one to share my grief, but there was no one, no comforter for me, and I found none.
They gave me gall for my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their table before them become a snare, a retribution, and a stumbling block.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they may not see, and bend their back continually.
Pour out your wrath upon them, and let the anger of your wrath overtake them.
Let their dwelling place be desolate, and let there be no inhabitant in their habitation;
Those whom you anointed [?], they persecuted him, and they added to the pain of your wounds.
Add iniquity to their iniquity, and let them not enter into your righteousness;
Let them be blotted out from the book of the living, and let them not be written with the righteous.
But I am poor and fallen, O God; your salvation has continually sustained me.
I will praise the name of the Lord my God with song, and I will exalt him with praise;
And I shall please God more than a young calf that puts forth horns and hooves.
Let the poor see and rejoice; let them seek God, and their souls shall live.
The Lord has heard the needy, and he does not despise his prisoners.
Praise him, heaven and earth, the sea and everything that is in it.
For the Lord will save Zion and will build the cities of Judea; they will settle there and inherit it;
and the offspring of the servants will inherit it; and those who love your name will dwell upon it.
O God, look to my help; O God, hasten to help me.
Let those who seek my soul be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who plot evil against me be turned back and put to shame.
Let those who said to me, "Aha, aha!" be turned back at once in shame.
Let all who seek you, O Lord, rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation say always: God is great!
But I am poor and needy; O God, help me. You are my helper and my deliverer; my God, do not make me wait.
In you, O Lord, I trust; let me not be put to shame forever.
In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me; incline your ear to me and save me.
Let God be my protector and a stronghold for my rescue; for you are my firmness and the one who makes me strong.
My God, deliver me from the hands of the sinner, from the hands of the lawless and the deceitful;
for you are my endurance, O Lord; the Lord is my hope from my youth.
On you I have been established from the womb; from my mother's belly you are my protector; my song is to you always.
I became like a portent to many; you are my helper and my strength.
Fill my mouth with praise, that we may sing of your glory, and all day long of the greatness of your beauty.
Do not cast me off, O Lord, in the time of old age, and when my strength fails do not forsake me.
For my enemies spoke to me, and those who surrounded my soul plotted together,
and they said: God has forsaken him; let us pursue him and overtake him, for there is no one to deliver him.
My God, do not go far from me; O Lord, hasten to help me.
Let those who slander my soul be ashamed and fail; let those who seek my harm put on shame and disgrace.
But I will always hope in you, and I will add to all your praise.
My mouth shall tell your righteousness, and all the day your salvation, for I do not know letters.
But I shall enter in the power of the Lord; O Lord, I have remembered your name alone.
My God, you taught me from my youth, and until now I shall recount your wonders.
Even to my advanced years and old age, my God, do not abandon me, until I recount your strong arm to every generation to come; your might
and your righteousness reach to the heights. How many great things you have done, O God; who shall be like you?
How many many afflictions and evils you have shown us; yet you turned and saved me, and brought me up from the abysses of the earth.
You multiplied your power; you turned and comforted me.
Now I too shall confess you with a prepared song of your truth, O God; I shall sing to you with blessing, O Holy One of Israel.
My lips shall rejoice when I sing to you, and my soul also, which you redeemed.
Moreover, my tongue too shall tell your righteousness, when all who seek evil for me are ashamed and disgraced.
O God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the son of the king,
to judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice.
Let the mountains receive peace for the people, and the hills righteousness,
to vindicate the poor of the people, to save the children of the fallen, and to humble the proud.
He shall stand and remain with the sun and before the moon, from generation to generation.
He shall come down like rain upon his fleece, and like dew that drips upon the earth.
In his days righteousness and much peace shall shine forth, until the moon is taken away [?].
He shall praise [?] him from sea to sea, and from the river to the end of the world.
Before him the Indians shall first fall down, and his enemies shall lick the dust.
The kings of Tarshish and of the islands shall offer gifts to him; the kings of Arabia and of Sheba shall bring gifts to him.
All the kings of the earth shall bow down to him, and every people shall serve him;
for he delivered the poor from the hands of the mighty, the afflicted and the fallen who had no helper.
He shall spare the poor and the fallen, and shall save the souls of the lowly.
From usury and falsehood he shall redeem their souls, and his name shall be glorified before them.
He shall live, and there shall be given to him of the gold of Arabia; they shall pray to him at all times and bless him every day.
Let it be a support in all the earth, and on the tops of the mountains its fruit shall be raised higher than Lebanon, and they shall flourish in your city like the grass of the earth.
Let his name be blessed forever, for his name is before it; by him all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed, and every generation shall call him blessed.
Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
And blessed is the holy name of his glory forever and forever and ever; and all the earth was filled with his glory. So be it, so be it.
How good is the God of Israel to the upright in heart.
But as for me, my feet were almost shaken; a little more and my steps would have gone astray.
For I was envious of the wicked, and I was watching the peace of sinners.
For there is no sin in their death, and their scourges are made firm;
They do not toil along with other people, and they are not tormented as other people are.
Therefore their pride has seized them completely; they clothed themselves with ungodliness and falsehood.
And their falsehoods came forth as if from fatness, for they walked in the counsel of their heart.
They plotted and spoke wickedness, and they spoke falsehood loftily.
They set their mouths in the heavens, and their tongue trailed over the earth.
Therefore my people shall turn back here, and full days shall be found among them.
And I said: How has God perceived this? Or is there knowledge with the Most High?
Behold, thus the sinners prosper; they stand firm and hold the wealth of the world.
And I said: Surely in vain have I justified myself and washed my hands in purity.
I was tormented every day, and my reproof comes at dawn.
And I said: How shall I tell him this: Behold, I have made a promise to the generation of your children?
It came to my heart and I said: This too is toil before me,
until I enter the sanctuary of God and understand their end.
But because of their deceit you trampled them, and you cast them down through their pride.
How have they become desolate in that instant? They were crushed, they failed, and they perished through their lawlessness.
They have become like the dreams of those who wake; O Lord, in your city you have despised the record of their image.
For my heart blazed up like fire, and my kidneys were changed.
I was made contemptible and did not understand; I was reckoned like a beast before you.
And I am always with you; you have held my right hand.
And you guide me by your counsels; with your glory you have received me.
What is there laid up for me in the heavens? Or what have I asked of you upon the earth?
My heart and my flesh have failed, O God of my heart; God is my portion forever.
For is it not so, behold, that those who have removed themselves from you have perished? And all who have revolted from you were destroyed.
But as for me, drawing near to God is good, and placing my hope in the Lord, and telling all your praises at the gates of the daughter of Zion.
Why do you cast us away, O God, completely? Your wrath has been kindled against the sheep of your flock.
Remember your congregation, which you acquired from the beginning; you redeemed the portion of your inheritance, Mount Zion, on which you have dwelt.
Lift up your hand against their arrogance completely; how greatly has the enemy acted falsely against your holiness!
And those who hate you boasted in the midst of your feasts; they set up their signs as signs and did not know
the exits above.
As a tree in a forest, so they hewed down their gates with the axe; all together, with axe and pick, they brought them down.
They burned your holy place with fire, and on the ground they defiled the tent of your name.
They said in their heart, and their kindred together: Come, let us make the feasts of God cease from the earth.
For we have not seen a sign; no one is a prophet any more, and no one will know us.
How long, O Lord, will the enemy reproach you, and the adversary provoke your holy name?
Why do you turn away your hand, and your right hand, into your bosom completely?
But God, our King, before creation, you wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.
You established the sea by your power; you crushed the heads of the dragons in the waters.
You crushed the heads of that dragon and gave it as food to the people of India.
You made springs and rivers flow forth; you dried up the mighty rivers.
Yours is the day and yours is the night; you established light and the sun.
You established all the boundaries of the earth; you created summer and spring.
Remember this, that the enemy reproached the Lord, and a foolish people provoked your holy name.
Do not give over to the beasts the soul that confesses you, and do not forget the soul of your poor altogether.
Look upon your covenant, for the houses of the lawless have been filled with the [?] of the land.
Let not the lowly one turn back ashamed; let the poor and the fallen bless your name.
Arise, O God, judge your cause; remember the reproach against you that comes from the foolish every day.
Do not forget the voice of those who pray to you; the arrogance of those who hate you has risen up continually.
We will confess you, O God, we will confess you and call upon your name; I will recount all your wonders,
when I take up the time, and I will judge righteousness.
The earth and all its inhabitants have melted away, and I have made its pillars firm.
I said to the lawless: Do not act lawlessly any more; you sinners, do not lift up your heads;
do not raise your horns on high, nor speak falsehood about God.
For not from the east, nor from the west, nor from the deserts of the mountains,
but God is the judge: this one he humbles and this one he exalts,
for the cup in the hands of the Lord is full of unwatered wine, poured in; it has tilted from here to there, yet its dregs will not run out; all the sinners of the earth will drink it.
But I will rejoice in the Lord and sing praise to the God of Jacob.
All the horns of sinners have been broken, and the horn of their [?] will be exalted.
God is made manifest in Judea, and over Israel his name is great.
May his place be in peace and his dwelling in Zion.
For there the Lord broke the powers of the bows, the armor and the sword and the battle.
You give light wondrously from the mountains forever.
All the foolish in heart were shaken; they slept their sleep, and all their fathers did not find the wealth of their hand.
At your wrath, O God of Jacob, those who sat upon horses fell into slumber.
You are terrible, O Lord, and who can stand before you? Your wrath is from the beginning.
When you appeared from heaven, you made your judgments manifest; the earth was afraid and trembled,
when God rose up for judgment, to deliver all the meek of the earth.
The thought of man will confess you, and the hidden things of wisdom will sing praise to you.
Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord your God, all you who are around him; offer gifts
to the Terrible One, who takes away the spirits of rulers; he is more terrible than all the kings of the earth.
With my voice I cried out to God, with my voice to God, and he looked upon me.
In the day of my affliction I sought God, with my hands, by night, before him, and I did not go astray; comfort was taken away from my soul.
I remembered God and rejoiced; I was anxious, and my soul grew faint.
My eyes reached the night watch ahead of time; I was shaken and did not speak.
I pondered the former days, and the eternal years
I remembered, and I pondered: by night I was anxious in my heart, and my spirit searched me.
Will the Lord indeed cast me off, and no longer show me his favor?
Or will he withhold his mercy from me completely, and carry out his word from generation to generation?
Or will he forget to accept me, and withhold his compassion in his anger?
And I said: Now I have begun, for this is the renewal from the right hand of the Most High.
I remembered the works of God, for I remembered your wonders from the beginning.
I spoke of all your works, and I pondered the creation, the work of your hands.
O God, your ways are in the holy place; who is a great god like our God?
You are the God who did wonders; you made your power known to your people.
With your arm you redeemed your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph.
The waters saw you, O God, the waters saw you and were afraid; the depths trembled
with a great roaring of water. The clouds gave voice, for your arrows go forth.
The voice of your thunder was in the wheel; your lightnings appeared; the world saw, and the earth trembled.
Your ways are on the sea, your paths on many waters, and your footprints are not known.
You led your people like sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Give heed, my people, to my judgment; incline your ear to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in a parable, and I will speak parables from the beginning.
All that we have heard, we have come to know it, and our fathers told it to us.
It was not hidden from their children for another generation, to tell the praises of the Lord, his powers and his wonders that he did.
He established his testimony in Jacob and gave his law over Israel, which he once commanded their fathers to make known to their children,
so that another generation might know this; the children who would be born would arise and tell this to their children,
so that they might set their hope on God, and not forget the works of God, and seek out his commandments,
so that they might not be like all their fathers, a perverse and embittering generation, a generation that did not set its heart right and did not make its spirit steadfast toward God.
The sons of Ephraim, mighty men and strong archers, turned back on the day of battle.
They did not keep the covenant of God and did not wish to walk in his judgment.
They forgot the benefits of God, his powers and his wonders that he showed them,
the wonders he did before their fathers in the land of Egypt and in the plain of Tanis.
For he split the sea and led them through, and he made the waters stand as if in skins [?].
He led them with a cloud by day, and all night with the light of fire.
He split the rock in the wilderness and gave them drink as if from a great deep.
He brought forth springs from the rock, and the waters came pouring down like rivers.
But they added still further to their sin; they embittered the Most High in the waterless land.
And they tested God in their hearts by demanding food for themselves.
They murmured against God and said: Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?
He struck the rock, and waters came out and rivers flowed; can he not also give bread, or prepare a table for his people?
Therefore the Lord heard and grew angry; fire was kindled against Jacob, and wrath rose up against Israel,
because they did not believe in God, nor did they hope in his salvation.
He commanded the clouds from above and opened the doors of heaven.
He rained manna on them to eat; he gave them the bread of heaven.
Man ate the bread of angels; he sent them food in abundance, to satisfy them fully.
He raised up a wind [?] from heaven and sent it out by his power from the north.
He rained flesh on them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea.
They fell in the midst of their camp and all around their tents.
They ate and were greatly filled; he gave them what they desired.
And he did not deprive them of their desire; the food was still in their mouths,
and the wrath of God rose up against them; he slew many of them and laid low the chosen of Israel.
For all this they sinned, and still they did not believe in his wonders.
Their days wasted away in vanity, and their years passed away in haste.
Whenever he slew them, then they would seek him; they would turn back and rise early to come to God.
They would remember that God is their helper, and that the Lord God Most High is their redeemer.
They loved him greatly with their mouths, and with their tongues they lied to him.
But their hearts were not upright toward him, nor did they believe in his covenant.
But he himself was merciful; he forgave their sins and did not destroy them. Many times he turned away his anger and did not kindle all his wrath.
He remembered that they are flesh, a breath that goes away and does not return.
How many times they embittered him in the desert and tested God in the waterless land!
They turned back and tested God Most High, and they angered the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his hand on the day when he redeemed them from the hands of their oppressors;
how he set his miracles in Egypt and his signs in the plain of Tanis;
he turned their rivers and their rain into blood, so that they could not drink;
he sent the dog-fly among them, and it devoured them, and with the frog he destroyed them.
He gave their fruit to venom and their labor to the locust;
he struck their vineyards with hail and their fig trees with frost;
he gave their flocks to the hail and their possessions to fire;
he sent upon them the wrath of his anger; anger, wrath and affliction he sent among them by the hand of a wrathful angel;
he made a way for the places of his wrath and did not spare their souls from death, and he shut up their flocks to famine.
He slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, the beginning of all their labor, from the dwellings of Ham;
he led forth his people like sheep and brought them out like a flock into the desert.
He guided them in hope, and they did not fear, and the sea covered their enemies.
He brought them to the mountain of his holiness, this mountain which his right hand had acquired.
He drove out the nations from before his face and apportioned to them a lot of inheritance; he settled the tribes of Israel in their dwellings.
They tested and embittered God Most High, and they did not keep his testimonies.
Then they turned back and acted falsely toward him, like all their fathers, and they were twisted aside like a crooked bow.
They provoked him to anger with their high places, and with their idols they moved him to jealousy.
The Lord heard and was angered, and he greatly despised Israel.
He cast away from himself the tent of Shiloh, the tent which had dwelt among men.
He gave their strength into captivity and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.
He delivered his people over to the sword and disregarded his inheritance.
Fire devoured their young men, and no one mourned for their virgins.
Their priests fell by the sword, and no one wept for their widows.
The Lord awoke like one who had been sleeping, and like a mighty man who shakes off wine.
He struck down his enemies backward; he made them an everlasting reproach.
He removed from himself the tent of Joseph and did not choose the seed of Ephraim,
but he chose the seed of Judah and Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his sanctuary like that of the unicorn; he established it upon the earth forever.
He chose David his servant and took him up from the flocks of sheep,
and from among the young of the lambs he brought him out to shepherd Jacob his servant and Israel his inheritance.
He shepherded them in the blamelessness of his heart, and in the innocence of his hands he led them.
O God, the nations have entered your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem like the bed of those who guard fruit.
They have laid out the corpses of your servants as food for the birds of the sky, and the flesh of your holy ones for the beasts of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
We have become a reproach to our brethren, a laughingstock and an object of scorn to those around us.
How long, O Lord, will you be utterly angry, and will your jealousy blaze up like fire?
Pour out your wrath upon the nations who do not know you, and upon the kings who do not call upon your name.
For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place.
Do not remember our former iniquities; but let your mercy quickly come to our aid, O Lord, for we have become exceedingly poor.
Help us, O God our Savior, for the glory of your name; O Lord, deliver us and be merciful to us concerning our sins for your name's sake.
Let the nations not say: "Where is their God?" But be made manifest among the nations before our eyes, to seek vengeance for the blood of your servants that was shed.
Let the sighing of those in fetters come in before you, and by the wealth of your arm help the children of the slain.
Repay into the bosoms of those around us sevenfold their reproach, with which they have reproached you, O Lord.
But we, your people and the sheep of your flock, will give thanks to you forever, and from generation to generation we will recount your praise.
You who shepherd Israel, look upon us, you who lead Joseph like a sheep, you who sit upon the cherubim, be made manifest
before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh; raise up your power and come to save us.
O God of hosts, turn us back, show your face upon us, and we shall be saved.
O Lord God of hosts, how long will you be angry at the prayer of your servant?
You feed us bread with tears, and you give us tears to drink by measure;
You have made us a reproach to those around us, and our enemies scorn us.
O Lord God of hosts, turn us back, show your face upon us, and we shall be saved.
You moved a vine out of Egypt, you drove out the nations and planted it.
You went before it, you made its roots firm, and it filled the land.
Its shade covered the mountains, and its tendrils the firs of God.
It stretched out its branches to the sea, and its shoots to the river.
Now why have you pulled down its wall, so that all who pass along the road gather its grapes?
The boar from the forest has ravaged it, and the fierce wild beast has grazed it away.
O God of hosts, turn now, look down from heaven and take thought, and look upon this vine.
Make firm this which your right hand has planted, and upon the son of man whom you have strengthened for yourself.
Burned with fire and laid waste, they shall perish at the wrath of your face.
Let your hand be upon the man, and your right hand upon the son of man whom you have strengthened for yourself.
We have not departed from you; but save us, and we will call upon your name, O Lord.
O Lord God of hosts, turn us back, show your face upon us, and we shall be saved.
Sing to God, our helper; shout to the God of Jacob.
Take up a psalm and give him blessing; sing to him with a sweet voice.
Sound [?] the new trumpet at the beginning of the month, on the feast of our rest.
For this is commanded for Israel, and it is a judgment [?] of the God of Jacob.
He set this as a testimony with Joseph, when he came out of the land of Egypt. He heard a language that he did not know.
He removed his shoulders from the burden, and his hands from slavery with the basket.
Should you call on me in distress, I will deliver you and hear you in the hidden places of the storm. I tested you at the waters of contention.
Hear, my people, and I will testify to you; and, Israel, if you would hear me,
let there be no transient god for you, nor shall you worship a foreign god.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt; open your mouth, and I will fill it.
My people did not hear my voice, and Israel did not heed me.
I let them go on in the will of their own selves, so that they might walk in the will of their heart.
If my people had heard me, and if Israel had been perfect in my ways,
I would have humbled his enemies as if they were nothing, and I would have laid my hand upon his oppressors.
The enemies of the Lord lied to him, and their time will be forever.
He fed them from the fatness of wheat, and from the rock he satisfied them with honey.
God stood in the assembly of the gods, and in the midst of the gods he judged them.
How long will you judge falsely and show partiality to persons, you sinners?
Give judgment for the orphan and the widow; vindicate the lowly and the poor.
Rescue the poor and the fallen; deliver him from the hands of the sinner.
They did not know, nor did they understand, for they walked in darkness; therefore all the foundations of the earth were shaken.
I said: You are indeed gods, or sons of the Most High, all of you;
but you, behold, will die like men and fall like one of the princes.
Arise, O God, judge the earth, for you will inherit all the nations.
O God, who is like you? Do not keep silent, and do not be still, O God.
For behold, your enemies have cried out, and those who hate you have lifted up their head.
Against your people they have schemed [?] with cunning, and they have plotted against your holy ones;
and they said: Come, let us destroy them from among the tribes, and let the name of Israel be remembered no more.
For they have plotted in conspiracy with one another, and concerning you they have made a covenant:
the camp of the Edomites and the Ishmaelites, Moab, the Hagarites,
Gebal, Ammon and Amalek, those foreign tribes, all dwelling in Tyre;
and Assyria too had come with them; all these had come as a strength to the sons of Lot.
My God, make them like Midian, Sisera, and like Jabin at the brook of Kishon.
Let them be destroyed at Endor; let them become like the dung of the earth.
Make their rulers like Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna, all their rulers,
who said: Come, let us take possession for ourselves of the holy place of God.
My God, make them like the wheels of a cart and like reeds before the wind.
As fire burns up the forests, and as flame burns up the mountains,
so pursue them with your storm wind, and with your wrath make them tremble.
Fill their face with disgrace, and let them seek your name, O Lord.
Let them be ashamed and tremble forever and ever, and, filled with shame, let them perish.
Let them know that your name is Lord, and that you alone are Most High over all the earth.
For beloved are your dwellings, O Lord God of hosts!
My soul longs and faints for the courts of the Lord. My heart and my flesh rejoice in the living God.
For even the sparrow has found a home, and the turtledove has placed her young in a nest: your altar, O Lord God of hosts, my King and my God.
Blessed are those who dwell in your house; forever and ever they shall praise you.
Blessed is the man whose help is from you. He has set an ascent in his heart,
in the valley of mourning, at the place that he promised, for he who gave the law has given a blessing.
They shall go from strength to strength; the God of gods shall appear to them in Zion.
Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob.
You are my helper; behold, O God, and look upon the face of your anointed.
For one day in your courts is better than those thousands; I have chosen to lie cast down at the house of God rather than to dwell in the dwelling of sinners.
The Lord our God loves mercy and truth. He will give grace and glory; the Lord will not withhold his good from those who walk blamelessly.
Lord God of hosts, blessed is the man who trusts in you.
You have been pleased, Lord, with your land; you have turned back the captivity of Jacob.
You have forgiven the iniquity of your people and covered all their sins.
You have calmed all your anger; you have turned back from the wrath of your anger.
Turn to us, O God our Savior, and turn your wrath away from us.
Do not be angry with us forever, and do not prolong your wrath from generation to generation.
O God, turn and save us, and we your people shall rejoice in you.
Show me, Lord, your mercy, and give us your salvation.
Let us hear whatever the Lord our God will say, for he spoke peace to his people, to his holy ones, and also to those who have turned to him in heart.
For his salvation is near to those who fear him, that his glory may dwell in our land.
Mercy and truth have met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
Truth has sprung up from the earth, and righteousness has appeared from heaven.
For the Lord will give sweetness, and our land will yield its fruit.
Righteousness shall go before him, and he shall set his way for walking.
Incline your ear, Lord, and hear me, for I am only-begotten and poor.
Guard my soul, for you are holy; save your servant, my God, who trusts in you.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I cry to you all the day.
Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul.
For you, Lord, are sweet and righteous, and you are greatly merciful to all who call upon you.
Give ear, O God, to my supplication, and attend to the voice of my prayer.
On the day of my distress I called upon you, and you heard me.
There is no one like you among the gods, O Lord, and there is nothing like your works.
Let all the nations, as many as you have made, come and worship before you, O Lord, and let them glorify your name, O Lord,
for you are great, O Lord, and a doer of wonders; you alone are God.
Lead me, O Lord, in your ways, and I will walk in your truth; let my heart rejoice in the fear of your name.
I will give thanks to you, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify your name forever;
for great is your mercy upon me, and you have delivered my soul from the lowest hell.
O God, the lawless have risen up against me, and an assembly of the mighty has sought my soul; they have not regarded you as God before them.
And you, the Lord God, are compassionate and merciful, long-suffering, abundantly merciful and true.
Look upon me and have mercy on me; give strength to your servant and save the son of your handmaid.
Work a good sign with me, so that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, for you, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.
Its foundations are in the holy mountains.
The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things have been spoken of you, O city of God.
I have remembered Rahab and the Babylonian, who know me; behold, foreign peoples from Tyre and the people of the Indians, these were there.
A man will say to Zion, "Mother," for a man was born there, and he himself, the Most High, founded it.
The Lord recounted in a writing of the people and of the rulers who were in it,
so that all may be joyful whose dwelling is from you.
O Lord God of my life, by day and by night I have cried out before you;
let my prayer come in before you. Incline your ear to my supplication,
for my soul is filled with evils, and my life has drawn near to hell.
I have been counted with those who go down into the pit; I have become like a man without help,
free among the dead, like the slain who sleep in the graves, whom you have not remembered, and they have been removed from your hand.
They have laid me in the lowest pit, in darkness and in the shadows of death.
Upon me you have made your anger firm, and you have brought all your [?] upon me.
You have removed those who know me far from me; you have made me an object of reproach to them; I was handed over and could not come out.
My eyes have failed because of my poverty. I have cried out to you, Lord, and every day I have lifted up my hands to you.
Will you not do wonders for the dead? Or will physicians raise them up, and will they confess you?
Will anyone tell of your mercy in the graves, or of your truth in the place of destruction?
Will your wonders not be known in the darkness, or your righteousness in that forgotten land?
But I have cried out to you, Lord, and at dawn my prayers will come before you.
Why, Lord, do you put my soul far from you? Or why do you turn your face away from me?
I am poor and in toil from my youth; from my height I have been brought low and have grown faint.
Your wrath has been made strong upon me, and your terrors have made me tremble.
They surrounded me like waters all day long and closed in on me all together.
You have removed from me friends, neighbors, and my acquaintances because of my poverty.
I will sing of your mercies, Lord, forever; from generation to generation I will declare your truth with my mouth.
For you said: I will build the world with mercy, and in the heavens I will establish my truth.
I made a covenant with my chosen ones and swore an oath to David my servant:
I will establish his offspring forever and build up his throne from generation to generation.
The heavens will confess your wonder, Lord, and your truth in the assembly of the saints.
For who is there in the clouds who is equal to the Lord? Or who among the sons of God will be like the Lord?
God is glorious in the council of the saints; he is great and terrible over those who are around him.
Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are mighty, Lord, and your truth is all around you.
You rule over the might of the sea, and you calm the roar of its waves.
You have brought low the proud like the wounded; with the strength of your arm you have scattered your enemies.
Yours are the heavens and yours is the earth; you have founded the world and all that fills it.
You created the north and the south; Tabor and Hermon will rejoice in your name.
Yours is the arm and yours is the might; let your hand be strong and your right hand be lifted high.
Your throne is set up in righteousness and judgment; mercy and truth will go before you.
Blessed is the people that knows your praise; Lord, they will walk in the light of your face.
In your name they shall rejoice all the day, and in your righteousness they shall be exalted.
For you are the boast of their strength, and by your will their horn shall be exalted.
For help is from the Lord, and from the Holy One, O Israel, your King.
Then you spoke in a vision to your offspring and said: I have laid help upon a mighty one, and I will exalt the chosen one of my people.
I have found David, my servant, and with my holy anointing oil I have anointed him.
My hand shall support him, and my arm shall strengthen him.
His enemy shall gain no advantage over him, and the son of lawlessness shall not harm him.
I will strike down his enemies before him, and I will humble those who hate him.
My mercy and my truth are with him, and by my name his horn shall be exalted.
I will set his hand upon the sea and his right hand upon the rivers.
He shall call to me: You are my Father, God, the supporter of my life.
I will make him firstborn, higher than all the kings of the earth.
Forever I will keep my mercy for him, and I will make my covenant sure to him.
I will establish his descendants forever and ever, and his throne like the days of heaven.
And if his sons forsake my law and do not walk in my judgments,
if they treat my statutes with contempt and do not keep my commandments,
I will punish their iniquities with the rod and their sins with scourging;
but I will not withhold my mercy from him, nor will I be false to my truth,
nor will I profane my covenant, and what has come forth from my lips I will not alter.
Once I swore to David by my holiness, and I will not lie.
His descendants shall remain forever, and his throne shall be like the sun before me,
like the moon established forever; the faithful witness is in heaven.
But now you have put away, treated with contempt, and cast from you your anointed one.
You have overturned the covenant of your servant and profaned his holiness upon the earth.
You have broken down all his walls and made his stronghold tremble;
All who pass along the road plundered him, and he has become a reproach to his neighbors.
You have raised the right hand of his oppressors and made all his enemies rejoice;
You have turned back the help of his sword and did not help him in battle.
You have defiled his holiness and cast his throne down to the ground;
You have shortened the days of his times and spread shame over him.
How long, O Lord? Will you be angry to the utmost, and will your jealousy blaze up like fire?
But now remember and see: what is our strength? Or have you indeed made all the sons of men in vain?
Who is the man who will live and not see death, or who will deliver his soul from the hands of hell?
Where are your former mercies, O Lord, which you swore to David in your truth?
Remember the reproach of your servants, which I have gathered into my bosom from many peoples;
With which your enemies have reproached me, O Lord, with which they have reproached me in place of your anointed.
Blessed is the Lord God forever. So be it, so be it.
O Lord, you have been a refuge for us from generation to generation.
Before the mountains were yet created and the earth and all the world were made, from everlasting to everlasting you are.
Do not turn men back to lowliness; you said: Turn back, sons of men.
For a thousand years in the eyes of the Lord are like yesterday, which has passed, and like one watch of the night.
Their years were held in contempt; at dawn they spring up like green grass,
At dawn like green grass they rejoice and blossom; at evening they wither and dry up and fall.
For we have wasted away by your wrath, and by your anger we were dismayed.
We have set our sins before you, and our life in the light of your face.
For all our days have wasted away and by your wrath we were dismayed; the time of our years is unstable, like a spider's web.
The number of the days and years of ours is at most seventy years, if more, eighty years, and the greater part of them is toil and pain; for gentleness has come upon us, and we have been instructed.
Who then will know the power of your wrath, or who will number your anger out of fear of you?
Thus show your right hand, O Lord, to the humble and to those instructed in heart: your wisdom.
Turn back, O Lord! How long? And comfort your servants.
We were filled in the morning with your mercy; may we rejoice and be glad all the days of our life,
in place of those days in which you humbled us, and those years in which we saw hardship.
Look upon your servants, Lord, and upon the work of your hands, and guide their sons.
May the light of the Lord our God be upon us; direct the works of our hands for us, Lord, and make the work of our hands prosper for us.
He who dwells in the help of the Most High shall rest in the shelter of God in heaven.
He shall say to the Lord: You are the one who holds me by the hand, my refuge, my God, and I trust in him.
For he has delivered me from the snare of the hunters and from the terrifying word.
With the space between his shoulders he will shelter you, and in the shadow of his wings you will hope; like armor his truth will surround you.
You shall not be afraid of the terror of the night, nor of the arrow that flies by day,
of the affliction that walks in darkness, of the assault of the demon at midday.
Thousands shall fall at your left and tens of thousands at your right, but they shall not come near you.
But you shall look with your eyes and see the recompense of sinners.
For you, Lord, are my hope; you have made the Most High a refuge for me.
Evil shall not come in to you, and no scourge shall come near your dwellings.
For he has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
With their arm they shall lift you up, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.
You shall walk upon the asp and the viper, and you shall trample the lion and the dragon.
For he has trusted in me, I will deliver him and be his protector, for he has known my name.
He shall call to me and I will hear him; I will be with him in affliction.
I will deliver him and glorify him with long life; I will satisfy him and show him my salvation.
It is good to confess the Lord and to sing to your name, Most High;
to tell of your mercy in the morning and of your truth at night,
with the ten-stringed psaltery and with the voice of blessing, praise;
for you have gladdened us with your creation, and in the work of your hands we shall rejoice,
for your works have become great, Lord, and your thoughts are very deep.
A foolish man will not know this, and the senseless will not understand this.
The springing up of sinners is like grass, and so is the appearing of those who do lawlessness, so that they may be destroyed forever and ever.
But you are on high forever, O God.
For behold, your enemies, O Lord, for behold, your enemies have perished, and all who do lawlessness will be scattered.
My horn will be exalted like that of a unicorn, my old age with oil and richness.
My eye will see what becomes of my enemies, and my ear will hear of those who have risen up against me with evil.
The righteous will flourish like a palm tree and will multiply like a fir of Lebanon.
They are planted in the house of the Lord; they will flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
Moreover, they will multiply in a rich old age; they will be flourishing and tender in the telling.
For the Lord our God is upright, and there is no falsehood in him.
The Lord reigns; he has clothed himself with beauty. The Lord has clothed himself with strength and girded himself. He has established the world, so that it will not be shaken.
Your throne is prepared, O God, from the ages, and you are forever.
The rivers have risen, O Lord. The rivers have lifted up their voice; the rivers have risen up in their course.
With the voice of many waters, wonderful are the surgings of the sea; wonderful are you in the heights, O Lord.
Your testimonies have become very sure; holiness befits your house, O Lord, for length of days.
God is the seeker of vengeance; the Lord God is the seeker of vengeance, and he has appeared openly.
Be exalted, O judge of righteousness, and render to the proud their recompense.
How long will sinners, O Lord, how long will sinners boast?
They pour forth and speak falsehood; all who do lawlessness speak it.
They have humbled your people, O Lord, and have afflicted your inheritance;
they have killed the widow and the stranger and slaughtered the orphans;
they have said: The Lord will not see this, nor will the God of Jacob understand this.
Understand now, you wicked among the people, and you senseless ones, understand at last.
He who planted the ears, does he not hear? Or he who made the eyes, does he not see?
He who instructs the nations, will he not also reprove, he who taught men knowledge?
The Lord knows the thoughts of people, that they are vain.
Blessed is the man whom you instruct, O Lord, and whom you teach from your law.
You give him calm from evil days, until a pit is dug for the sinner.
For the Lord will not cast off his people, and he will not disregard his inheritance,
until judgments turn back to righteousness, and all who are upright in heart will accept it.
Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Or who will stand with me against those who commit lawlessness?
Had the Lord not helped me, in a little [?] my soul would have come to dwell in hell.
If I said, "Behold, my feet have been shaken," the mercy of the Lord helped me.
In the many pains of my heart, your consolations gladdened my soul.
Let not the throne of lawlessness be made equal to you, which creates toil by decree.
They hunt the soul of the righteous and condemn innocent blood.
The Lord became my strengthener, God the helper of my hope.
The Lord will repay them for their lawlessness, and for the wickedness of their ways the Lord our God has destroyed them.
Come, let us sing to the Lord, let us cry out to God our Savior.
Let us rise early to come before his face with confession, and let us cry out to him with psalms.
For God is great, the Lord, and the King is great over all the earth;
for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the height of the mountains is his.
The sea is his, and he made it, and his hands created the dry land.
Come, let us worship, let us fall down and weep before the Lord our Maker.
For he is God our Savior, and we are the people of his flock and the sheep of his hand.
Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts in embitterment, as on that day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me; they tested me and saw my works.
For forty years, therefore, I was wearied by that generation, and I said, "They always go astray in their heart, and they have not known my ways."
As I swore in my wrath, they shall not enter my place of rest.
Sing to the Lord a new song, sing to the Lord, all the earth.
Sing to the Lord, bless his name, proclaim the good news of his salvation day after day.
Tell the nations of his glory, and every people of his wonders.
For the Lord is great and greatly praised, and he is terrible above all idols;
for all the idols of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens.
Thanksgiving and splendor are before him; holiness and great beauty are in his holiness.
Offer to the Lord, you tribes of the nations, offer to the Lord glory and honor;
offer to the Lord glory for his name; take up sacrifices, and enter his courts;
worship the Lord in his holy court. Let all the earth tremble before his face!
Say among the nations that the Lord reigns, for he has established the world so that it will not be shaken; he will judge his people with uprightness.
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth sing; let the sea be stirred with all that fills it.
Let the fields rejoice and everything that is in them; then all the trees of the forest will rejoice
before the face of the Lord, for he is coming, for he has come to judge the earth; he will judge the world with righteousness and the people with his truth.
The Lord reigns, let the earth rejoice, let the many coastlands be glad.
Cloud and mist are around him; his throne is set up with righteousness and ordering.
Fire goes before him, and his enemies around him were burned up.
His goings appeared to the world; the earth saw and trembled.
The mountains melted like wax before the face of the Lord, before the face of the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens told of his righteousness, and all the people saw his glory.
Let all be ashamed who worship things made by hands and who boast of their idols. Worship him, all you his angels.
Zion heard and rejoiced, and the daughters of Judea were glad because of your judgments, O Lord.
For you, the Lord, are high over all the earth; you are greatly exalted above all idols.
You who love the Lord, hate wickedness; the Lord has guarded the souls of his holy ones, and he will deliver them from the hand of the sinner.
Light has shone upon the righteous, and joy upon the upright of heart.
Let the righteous rejoice in the Lord, and give thanks to the memorial of his holiness.
Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done wonders. His right hand and his holy arm have saved him.
The Lord has shown his salvation; before the nations he has revealed his righteousness.
He has remembered his mercy toward Jacob and his truth toward the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
Cry out to God, all the earth; sing, rejoice, and give praise.
Sing to our God with blessing, with song, and with the voice of a psalm.
With the voice of blessing, with hammered trumpets, with blessing and the sound of the horn trumpet, cry out before the Lord the King.
Let the sea be stirred with its fullness, the world and all that is in it.
The rivers have lifted up their voice together, the mountains rejoice before the Lord, for he is coming,
for he has come to judge the earth; he will judge the world with righteousness and the people with uprightness.
The Lord reigns; let the peoples be angered. He who sits upon the cherubim, let the earth be shaken.
The Lord is great and high in Zion, and he is awesome over all the peoples.
Let us confess your great name, for it is awesome and holy.
And the honor of the King loves justice; you have prepared uprightness, you have done judgment and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down at the footstool of his feet, for he is holy.
Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among those who call upon his holy name. They called upon the Lord, and he heard them,
and he spoke to them in a pillar of cloud; for they kept his testimonies and his commandments, which he gave them.
O Lord God of hosts, you heard them; O God, you were forgiving to them and an avenger over all their deeds.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down at his holy mountain, for the Lord our God is holy.
Cry out to God, all the earth,
serve the Lord with joy, let us enter before him with gladness.
Know that he himself is the Lord our God; he made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people and the sheep of his flock.
Let us enter his gates with confession and his courts with singing; confess him and praise his holy name,
for the Lord is sweet, for his mercy is forever, and his truth is from generation to generation.
With mercy and righteousness I will praise you, O Lord.
I will sing to you and give heed to the blameless way; when will you come to me? I walked in the blamelessness of my heart in the midst of my house.
I did not set before my eyes a deed of lawlessness, and I hated the transgressors of the law; the crooked of heart did not cling to me,
And the turning away of the wicked from me, I did not know.
Whoever spoke evil in secret against his neighbor, him I drove out; whoever was proud of eye and insatiable of heart, with him I did not eat bread.
My eyes are on the holy ones of the earth, that they may sit with me; whoever walked in a blameless way, he served me.
Whoever acts with pride shall not dwell within my house; whoever speaks falsehood shall not prosper before my eyes.
At dawn I destroyed all the sinners of the earth, that all the workers of lawlessness might be destroyed from the city of the Lord.
Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come in to you.
Do not turn your face away from me; on the day that I am in distress, incline your ear to me; and on the day that I call on you, hear me quickly.
For my days have failed like smoke, and my bones have dried up like dry kindling.
My heart has been struck like grass and has withered, for I have forgotten to eat my bread.
From the sound of my groaning my flesh has clung to my bones.
I have become like the pelican of the wilderness, and I was like an owl in a ruin.
I was sleepless and remained like a lone sparrow on a rooftop.
All day long my enemies reviled me, and those who praised me swore against me.
For I ate ashes like bread and mingled my drink with my tears,
because of the anger of your wrath, for you lifted me up and cast me down.
My days have passed away like shadows, and I have withered like grass.
But you, Lord, remain forever, and your remembrance is from generation to generation.
You will arise and have mercy on Zion, for the time of mercy on her, the time, has come.
For her stones were pleasing to your servants, and they will have compassion on her soil.
Let the nations fear your name, and the kings of the earth your glory.
The Lord shall build up Zion and shall appear in his glory.
For he has looked upon the prayer of the lowly and has not despised their petition.
Let this be written for another generation, and let a people yet to be created praise the Lord;
for he looked down from his holy height; the Lord looked down from heaven to earth,
to hear the prayer of his captives and to set free the children of the slain,
To tell in Zion the name of the Lord, and his praise in Jerusalem,
when the peoples gather together, and kings, to serve the Lord.
He answered him in the way of his strength: Tell me the fewness of my days.
And do not take me away at the midpoint of my days, for your years are from generation to generation.
In the beginning you, Lord, established the earth, and the heavens are the works of your hands.
They will pass away, but you remain forever. All of them will grow old like garments, and you will change them like clothing, and they will be changed.
But you yourself are the same, and your years will not fail.
The sons of your servants will dwell in it, and their offspring will prosper forever.
My soul blesses the Lord, and all my mind blesses his holy name.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and do not forget all that he has given,
who forgave you your sins and who healed all your sickness;
who redeemed your life from corruption and crowned you with mercy and compassion;
who filled your desire with good things and renewed your youth like an eagle's.
The Lord will perform acts of mercy, and his judgments, for all the despised.
He showed his ways to Moses, and his commandments to the sons of Israel.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, long-suffering and greatly merciful.
The Lord will not be angry to the end, nor will he hold on to wrongdoing forever;
the Lord will not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities.
For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so has the Lord made his mercy strong upon those who fear him;
as far as the east is removed from the west, so has he removed our iniquities from us.
As a father has pity on his children, so the Lord has mercy on those who fear him.
For he knows how we were made; he remembered that we are earth.
As for man, his days are like grass, and like a flower of the field, so he blossoms;
the wind blows on it and it is no more, and its place can no longer be seen.
But the mercy of the Lord is from age to age upon those who fear him, and his righteousness to children's children,
those who keep his covenants, and remember his commandments and do them.
The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven, and his kingdom rules over all.
Bless the Lord, all you his angels, mighty in strength, who do his words, hearing the voice of his command.
Bless the Lord, all you his hosts, his servants, who do his will.
Bless the Lord, all you his works, in every place of his dominion; my soul blesses the Lord.
My soul blesses the Lord; O Lord my God, you have been greatly magnified; you have put on confession and great beauty,
you have clothed yourself with light as with a garment, you have stretched out the heavens like a tent;
he has roofed his upper chambers over the waters; he who has set the clouds as his ascent, and he moves upon the wings of the winds;
he who has made his angels spirit and his servants a flame of fire;
he who has established the earth on its firm foundation; it will not be shaken forever.
The abysses are laid around it like garments; the waters stand upon the mountains.
At your rebuke they flee, and at the voice of your [?] thunder they tremble.
They rise up and become mountains, they sink down and become [?] plains, at the place where you established them.
You have set a boundary and they do not pass over it, nor will they turn back to cover the earth.
He who sends forth springs among the ravines; the waters pass among the mountains;
they give drink to all the beasts of the field; the wild asses are satisfied in their thirst.
There the birds of the sky dwell, and from among the rocks they give forth their voice.
He who has made the mountains drunk from his treasury; with the fruit of the works of his hands he has filled the earth.
He who makes hay spring up for the mountains and green plants for the service of men, who brings forth bread from the earth.
Wine [?] gladdens the heart of man, oil makes the face cheerful, and bread strengthens the heart of man.
The trees of the Lord are satisfied, and the firs of Lebanon, which you have planted.
There the birds hatch their young, and the nest of the stork is counted among them.
The high mountains are for the deer, and the rocks are a refuge for the hares.
You have made the moon for the seasons; the sun has known the time of its setting.
He made darkness and it became night; in it all the beasts of the field walk about,
The lion cubs roar to seize prey, and they ask their food from God.
When the sun spreads forth, they gather and lie down in their own dens.
A man goes out to his work and to the labor of his hands until evening.
For great are your works, O Lord, and you have made everything in wisdom; the earth is filled with your creation.
Here is the great and wide sea; in it are all the creeping things, of which there is no number, small beasts together with great ones; upon it the ships go.
Here is this sea monster, which you created to be sported with by them.
All of them wait on you to give them their food in due time.
You give to them, and they are nourished; you lift up your hand and feed them all with the sweetness of your will.
You turn your face away from them, and they are shaken; you take their spirit from them, and they fail and return to their own earth.
You send forth your spirit, and you create them, and you renew the face of the earth.
May the glory of the Lord be forever; may the Lord rejoice over his works.
You who look upon the earth and make it tremble, who touch the mountains, and they smoke.
I will praise the Lord in my life; I will sing to my God as long as I exist.
May my blessing be sweet to him, and I will rejoice in the Lord.
May sinners vanish from the earth, and may the lawless no longer be found upon it. My soul blesses the Lord.
Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name; tell of his works among the nations.
Bless him and sing to him; tell of all his wonders that he has done.
Praise his holy name; rejoice, you hearts that seek the Lord.
Seek the Lord and be strengthened, and seek his face every day.
Remember his wonders that he has done, the signs and the judgments of his mouth.
You offspring of Abraham, his servants, you sons of Jacob and his chosen ones.
He himself is the Lord our God, and his judgments are over all the earth.
He has remembered his covenant forever, the word that he commanded to a thousand generations,
the covenant that he made with Abraham, and his oath with Isaac.
He confirmed his command with Jacob, and for Israel an everlasting covenant.
He said to them, "To you I will give the land of Canaan as the portion of your inheritance,"
for they were few in number, very few, and sojourners in it.
They went from generation to generation, and from kings to another people.
He did not allow anyone to harm them; he rebuked kings on their account and said:
"Do not touch my anointed one, and do not harm my prophet."
He called down famine on the land, and all the strength of bread was broken.
He sent a man before them, and Joseph was sold as a slave.
They humbled his feet with fetters; his body went into chains,
until his word came to pass; the word of the Lord tested him.
The king sent and released him, and as ruler of the people he set him free.
He set him as lord over his house and ruler over all his possessions,
to instruct his princes as himself, and the elders, so that he might make them wise.
Israel entered Egypt, and Jacob settled in the land of Ham.
He increased his people greatly and made them stronger, greater than all their enemies.
He turned their heart to hate his people and to deal treacherously with his servants.
He sent Moses his servant and Aaron his chosen one.
He gave them the words of his miracles and his signs in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness upon them and darkened them, for they embittered his words.
He turned their rivers into blood and killed their fish.
Their land teemed with frogs, in the treasuries of their kings.
He spoke, and there came the dog-fly and gnats in all their territories.
He turned their rain into hail, and fire blazed up in their land.
He destroyed their vineyards and their fig groves and shattered every tree of their territory.
He spoke, and there came locusts and flies without number.
They devoured the grass of their land and destroyed all their fruit.
He struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, the beginning of all their labor.
He brought them out with gold and silver, and there was no one sick among their tribe.
Egypt rejoiced at their departure, for a great fear had fallen upon them.
He spread out clouds to shade them by day, and with fire he gave them light by night.
They asked, and he gave them quail, and he filled them with the bread of heaven.
He struck the rock, and waters came forth, and rivers ran through the waterless land.
He remembered his holy word, which he had spoken with Abraham his servant.
He brought out his people with joy and his chosen ones with gladness.
He gave them the lands of the nations and settled them in the labor of the people,
so that they might keep his judgments and seek out his law.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is sweet, for his mercy endures forever.
Who could tell the mighty deeds of the Lord and make all his praises heard?
Blessed are those who keep his judgments and do his righteousness at all times.
Remember us, O Lord, with the favor shown to your people, and look upon us with your salvation,
so that we may see the sweetness with your chosen ones and rejoice in the joy of your nation, so that they may praise you together with your inheritance.
For we have sinned against you together with our fathers; we have become lawless and have turned away from you.
